key_insight: Deep reinforcement learning controls cylinder-mounted synthetic jets most effectively near flow separation regions, reducing drag and suppressing lift oscillations.
engineering_relevance: Optimizing jet placement could improve active flow-control performance and stability across increasing Reynolds numbers.
method: Use deep reinforcement learning to control cylinder-mounted synthetic jets.
Evaluate jet placement configurations across Reynolds numbers of 500, 1,000, and 2,000.
Apply multi-objective control targeting drag reduction and lift-oscillation suppression.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports drag reductions up to 37.4%, 49.1%, and 58.8% at Re = 500, 1,000, and 2,000, respectively, with complete vortex-shedding suppression at the two lower Reynolds numbers.
watch_item: Residual wake instabilities persist at Re = 2,000, so stability beyond the tested conditions remains uncertain.
paper_title: Optimizing synthetic jet placement for control stability in increasing Reynolds number flows based on deep reinforcement learning
